results.question: Contrast the identity checks in a TLS certificate with authorization checks on a private PDF.

evidence_diagnostics.excerpt: Authorization evaluates whether a caller may perform an action on a resource. For a private PDF, compare the verified caller identity with the document owner or an explicit sharing rule. Authentication is a prerequisite for authorization. Authorization is a prerequisite for document access control. These checks belong on the server and must cover previews, retrieval, downloads, deletion, and graph queries, even if the interface hides buttons.

Authentication establishes the identity of a caller using credentials or an existing session. Authorization decides whether that identity may perform a specific action on a resource. In this course authentication is a prerequisite for authorization, and authorization is a prerequisite for document access control. A successful login alone does not grant permission to every PDF in an application.

TLS protects data in transit using encryption and integrity checks. A certificate helps the client authenticate the server during the handshake. A browser checks that the certificate matches the requested hostname and chains to a trusted authority. TLS does not decide whether a signed-in user can read a particular document. HTTP is a prerequisite for studying TLS in this web course; TLS is a prerequisite for HTTPS.

Document access control enforces ownership or sharing rules on every operation involving a document. Its direct prerequisite is authorization; authentication is the foundational prerequisite before authorization. Protect vector searches and graph traversals with the same document scope used for PDF previews. Guessing an upload identifier must never grant access. HTTPS protects transport, but it cannot replace these resource permission checks.

HTTPS carries HTTP messages over TLS. To understand HTTPS, study TLS first and HTTP before TLS. This makes HTTP a foundational prerequisite two steps before HTTPS. HTTPS protects traffic between browser and server against passive reading and modification in transit. It does not repair application authorization bugs, prevent a malicious server from storing data, or guarantee that a website is honest.

An HTTP 401 response means authentication is required or the supplied credentials are not accepted. An HTTP 403 response means the request is forbidden; it can occur even when identity is known. HTTP 429 indicates too many requests and can include a Retry-After header. HTTP 503 indicates that a service is temporarily unavailable. Clients should distinguish these cases rather than report every failure as an invalid password.

HTTP defines requests and responses between a client and a server. A request contains a method, target, headers, and sometimes a body. A response contains a status code, headers, and optionally a body. HTTP itself does not encrypt the message. In this course, HTTP is a prerequisite for understanding TLS in web communication, and TLS is a prerequisite for understanding HTTPS. Learn this sequence: HTTP, then TLS, then HTTPS.

A signed session cookie lets a server detect tampering and verify an expiry time. HttpOnly prevents page JavaScript from reading the cookie; Secure restricts transmission to HTTPS. A signature provides integrity, not secrecy, so session contents must not include secrets that require encryption. A stateless signed cookie does not by itself create per-user document ownership or provide instant revocation without additional state.

Phishing uses deceptive messages or websites to persuade a person to disclose credentials or perform an unsafe action. A message may manufacture urgency to discourage checking the sender. Verify unexpected requests through a separate trusted channel. HTTPS can encrypt a phishing website's traffic, so a secure connection is not proof that the operator is trustworthy. This lesson distinguishes transport protection from human deception.

A database transaction groups related changes into a unit that commits or rolls back. For a document workflow, authoritative metadata can record which processing stage completed. A SQL transaction does not automatically roll back writes made to an external vector database or object store. In this course transactions are a prerequisite for idempotency, and idempotency is a prerequisite for safe retries.

methodology.scope: Authored PDFs with synthetic distractors; warm local models and in-memory Qdrant brute-force search.
limitations: No hosted ANN, HTTP, concurrency, PostgreSQL, or LLM generation benchmark.
Page-label precision is not human-verified passage relevance or generated-answer accuracy.
Source fragments are checked by exact text presence, not semantic correctness.
Validation cases were used to diagnose identifier failures; fresh held-out authored cases are separate and not independently annotated.
One warm sequential run per case; not a concurrency, uptime, or production-scale guarantee.
